Title: Project Engineering Manager, Staff
Industry: Semiconductor Manufacturing, Software Development, and Computer Hardware Manufacturing
Description:
We Are
  
  
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
  
  
What You'll Be Doing
  
  

* Own and maintain the integrated schedule and critical path across multiple Memory Interface IP development and release workstreams, from project kickoff and architecture through design closure, verification, customer delivery, and production readiness. Model dependency chains deeply enough to quantify the impact of slips and pull-ins, distinguish paths with float from those without it, and update the plan weekly using current engineering data.
* Drive the weekly project cadence by synthesizing inputs from architecture, RTL, design verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, packaging, software, infrastructure, product engineering, and post-silicon teams into a single view of program health, emerging concerns, and required actions.
* Track verification convergence and engineering maturity as leading indicators. Monitor feature readiness, RTL closure, bug discovery and closure trends, regression health, coverage, design maturity, and block-level readiness. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive a recovery plan before downstream milestones or customer commitments are affected.
* Analyze schedule scenarios and coordinate recovery plans. Work with engineering leads to understand technical constraints, resource limitations, and available float; quantify the impact of changes; develop practical options; and track agreed recovery actions to closure.
* Manage external partner and customer dependencies by owning delivery calendars, tracking execution plans and acceptance criteria, aligning technical dependencies, and supporting schedule negotiations with a clear understanding of downstream technical, commercial, and resource impacts.
* Lead cross-functional risk, issue, and decision management. Convert technical uncertainty into clear options, owners, dates, and decision points. Ensure risks, assumptions, and trade-offs are visible early and resolved at the appropriate level.
* Provide concise project insight to executives and customers. Distill complex engineering information into evidence-based updates that distinguish signal from noise, quantify schedule and delivery impact, and clearly identify the actions or decisions needed.

A Day In The Life
  
  
You start the morning reviewing verification-convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug-closure velocity has slowed. You bring the DV lead and RTL owner together for a focused sync, clarify the cause, and align on a recovery plan before the weekly project review.
  
  
In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects an internal delivery shift, quantify the downstream impact on release timing and customer commitments, and identify the decisions needed to protect the plan. Later, you follow-up with R&D on the strategy to take to resolve the issue, then finish the day preparing a concise executive summary and following up on owners and due dates from the project review.
  
  
What You'll Need
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Applied Science, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience, with 8+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor, silicon IP, SoC, ASIC, or complex hardware development.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex semiconductor or silicon IP programs across multiple engineering disciplines and geographically distributed teams.
* Strong working knowledge of semiconductor development lifecycles and the relationships among architecture, RTL, verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, software, infrastructure, and productization.
* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with meaningful dependency and critical-path modeling, including float analysis, milestone confidence, and the downstream effects of schedule changes.
* Experience using engineering evidence such as feature readiness, bug trends, regression results, coverage, design closure, and delivery health to assess schedule risk and drive corrective action.
* Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex technical and program information, develop practical options, and recommend a course of action.
* Strong communication and influence skills, including the ability to gain cooperation across engineering teams, customers, suppliers, and external partners and to present crisp status and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Experience with project and program management tools and data-driven reporting. Familiarity with Jira, schedule-management tools, dashboards, and engineering lifecycle metrics is preferred.
* Knowledge of quality-management processes and the ability to navigate Linux environments are considered assets.

Who You Are
  
  
This is not a status-reporting role. You will connect a broad set of engineering workstreams into a coherent, dependency-driven plan, identify the real critical path week to week, and drive the cross-functional actions and decisions that keep complex Memory Interface IP projects on track. The work spans concurrent development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, customers, external partners, and development infrastructure.
  
  
Working with general direction, you will apply strong semiconductor-development knowledge and program-management judgment to analyze issues, recommend practical solutions, and gain cooperation across teams. Success requires attention to engineering detail, disciplined follow-through, and the ability to turn complex technical inputs into clear priorities, ownership, and delivery commitments.
  
  
The Team You'll Be Part Of
  
  
Our engineering teams develop advanced Memory Interface IP that enables customers to build high-performance, differentiated SoCs. We work at the intersection of architecture, analog and mixed-signal design, RTL, verification, physical design, software, infrastructure, and customer deployment. The programs are technically complex, globally distributed, and tightly connected to customer and business commitments.
  
  
We value people who combine advanced technical judgment with clear communication, disciplined execution, and the willingness to work through details without losing sight of the broader outcome. In this role, you will help shape how complex semiconductor programs are planned and delivered, strengthen execution practices across teams, and work alongside talented engineers solving consequential problems at scale.
  
  
Rewards and Benefits
  
  
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

We are committed to provide access & opportunity to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodation to individuals throughout the recruitment and employment process. Should you require an accommodation, please contact hr-help-canada@synopsys.com.

Every day, we deliver safe and secure energy to homes, communities, and businesses, connecting people to the energy they need for their lives. To succeed, we must anticipate customer needs, reduce energy delivery costs, and pioneer flexible energy systems. This requires delivering on our promises and seeking opportunities for growth.

In IT and Digital, we collaborate closely with the diverse energy businesses within the National Grid group, revolutionizing operations through technology. Embracing modern methodologies and digital mindsets, we drive efficiency and bring new capabilities to internal and external customers as we lead the charge toward a carbon-free future.

Our work is critical, as National Grid powers millions of homes and businesses across the UK and US, and the technology we employ is vital to this task. The successful applicant for this position will play a crucial role in our mission, supported by our multicultural, customer-centric global team, with opportunities for professional development.

**National Grid is hiring a Head of US Operational Technology role which operates under a hybrid working model and is open to candidates based at our Waltham, MA, Syracuse, NY, and Brooklyn, NY.**

**This is a hybrid role. Employees are expected to work from their assigned office or another approved work location outside the home at least three days per week. Additional in-person attendance may be required based on role, team, and business needs.**

### **Job Purpose**

The Head of U.S. Operational Technology (OT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the safe, reliable, resilient, secure and supportable operation of the technology environments that underpin real-time electric transmission, electric distribution and gas distribution operations across Massachusetts and New York. The role reports to the VP, Head of IT&D Electric and works in close partnership with Electric and Gas Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Architecture, Regulatory, Capital Delivery and other enterprise technology leaders.

The role leads a multidisciplinary organization responsible for 24x7 operational support and lifecycle stewardship of OT applications and infrastructure. The scope includes Energy Management Systems (EMS), Gas Management System (GMS), Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS), Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), SCADA-related capabilities and the supporting network, compute, storage, database, integration and recovery environments. It also includes designated technology supporting LNG operations, physical security systems, substation controllers and substation access points.

You’ll join an established team, building on its existing strengths to deliver meaningful outcomes. Working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders, you’ll help shape priorities, improve ways of working, and support the team’s continued development and success.

The Head of OT leads directors responsible for application and infrastructure domains and is a key partner to control center, operations, regulatory and executive stakeholders. The role requires experienced, visible leadership during significant events; disciplined governance; strong technical judgment; and the ability to convert technical risk into clear business decisions.

### **Key Accountabilities**

**Safe, Reliable and Resilient Operations**

* Own the availability, resilience, performance, and recoverability of the OT estate.
* Establish clear 24x7 operational accountability, escalation, and decision-making.
* Lead technology response to major incidents and operational events.
* Maintain and test business continuity, disaster recovery, and recovery capabilities.
* Ensure readiness for storms, grid emergencies, outages, and critical operational events.
* Drive continuous improvement through incident analysis and root-cause elimination.

**Cybersecurity, Safety, Compliance and Risk**

* Maintain auditable controls, remediation plans, and risk management processes.
* Provide transparent reporting on operational, technology, and compliance risks.
* Support regulatory filings, rate cases, and investment planning.

**Technology Strategy and Lifecycle Stewardship**

* Drive risk-based management of patching, upgrades, vulnerabilities, capacity, and technical debt.
* Establish standards for integration, automation, observability, and platform management.
* Enable trusted operational data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

**Portfolio Prioritization and Investment Leadership**

* Own OT demand, capacity, and prioritization across operations and capital programs.
* Lead transparent prioritization and resource trade-off decisions.
* Maintain credible operational and capital forecasts.
* Translate technology investments into measurable business outcomes.
* Ensure effective governance, intake, and decision-making processes.

**Enabling Capital Delivery and Operational Acceptance**

* Align OT resources to the highest-priority initiatives.
* Represent operational requirements throughout delivery and implementation.
* Ensure operational readiness before service acceptance.
* Identify and manage cross-program dependencies and risks.
* Enable smooth transition from project delivery to steady-state operations.

**Team Leadership, Capability and Culture**

* Lead and develop senior leaders across OT applications and infrastructure.
* Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish role clarity across internal teams, partners, and suppliers.
* Build workforce capability, succession plans, and organizational resilience.
* Ensure teams are trained and prepared to meet operational and compliance obligations.
* Strengthen collaboration across OT, IT&D, Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, and Capital Delivery.

**Stakeholder, Executive and Vendor Leadership**

* Deep expertise in one or more OT domains (EMS, ADMS, DERMS, GMS, SCADA, OMS) with the ability to lead across a broader technology landscape.

Title: Shelter Manager

This position serves as the senior operational manager of Animal Orphanage and provides leadership, direction, and oversight of shelter-wide operations. The Shelter Manager is responsible for coordinating the work of the Animal Care Manager and other shelter employees, establishing operational priorities, and ensuring that organizational policies and procedures are consistently followed.

The Shelter Manager has overall operational authority and final day-to-day decision-making responsibility, subject to the authority of the Board of Directors. The Shelter Manager reports directly to the President and Vice President of the Board of Directors.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Shelter Operations and Administration

* Oversees the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of the shelter to ensure efficient and consistent operations.
* Provides overall operational leadership and direction to the Animal Care Manager and other shelter employees.
* Establishes organizational priorities and coordinates responsibilities between the Animal Care Manager and other staff to ensure effective shelter operations.
* Develops, implements, and monitors operational procedures and policies for staff and volunteers in collaboration with the Animal Care Manager.
* Ensures shelter operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, licensing requirements, and organizational policies.
* Responsible for the completion and submission of required administrative paperwork and documentation necessary to maintain applicable licenses, certifications, and regulatory compliance.
* Maintains accurate and organized administrative records, files, and documentation.
* Ensures shelter management software and applicable administrative records are current and maintained, coordinating with the Animal Care Manager regarding animal-related records.
* Oversees website administration and ensures public-facing shelter information is accurate and current.
* Coordinates with other shelters, rescues, municipalities, and outside organizations as needed.
* Develops and maintains positive working relationships with Animal Control, law enforcement, local veterinarians, volunteers, foster families, and other stakeholders.
* Ensures the public receives accurate, consistent, and professional information regarding shelter services, policies, and operations.

Staff Supervision and Human Resources

* Responsible for the overall supervision and administration of shelter employees.
* Oversees employee recruitment, hiring coordination, onboarding, and orientation in collaboration with the Board President and Vice President.
* Develops and maintains staff schedules and assigns work responsibilities to ensure adequate operational coverage.
* Establishes overall staffing priorities and coordinates scheduling with the Animal Care Manager.
* Monitors staffing levels and evaluates operational needs to ensure appropriate allocation of personnel.
* Evaluates the need to fill vacant positions and recommends changes to staffing structure and allocated positions as needed.
* Oversees employee performance management, including evaluations, coaching, corrective action, and documentation.
* Addresses employee relations matters and works to maintain a professional, respectful, and productive workplace.
* Coordinates staff training and ensures employees receive appropriate instruction regarding workplace policies, safety procedures, and job responsibilities.
* Monitors attendance, timekeeping, and employee leave records.
* Coordinates payroll submissions and related documentation with the bookkeeper.
* Communicates staffing concerns, performance issues, and significant personnel matters to the Board President or Vice President as appropriate.
* Works collaboratively with the Animal Care Manager to address animal care staffing needs, training, performance, and scheduling.
* Establishes clear supervisory responsibilities and ensures employees receive consistent direction and understand reporting relationships.

Financial and Administrative Coordination

* Works directly with the bookkeeper to coordinate and maintain accurate administrative and financial records.
* Coordinates payroll submissions, mileage reimbursements, employee time records, and other documentation required for bookkeeping and payroll processing.
* Tracks and monitors routine shelter expenses and communicates financial or purchasing concerns to the Board President or Vice President.
* Coordinates purchasing and maintains appropriate inventory of administrative supplies, office equipment, and general facility supplies.
* Works with the Animal Care Manager to coordinate animal care supply and equipment purchasing needs.
* Ensures purchases are made in accordance with established budgets, purchasing procedures, and Board authorization requirements.
* Maintains accurate records of purchases, invoices, receipts, deposits, and other administrative transactions.
* Assists with budget preparation, expense tracking, and financial reporting as requested.
* Receives, processes, and records donations and other payments, including entering donation information into the organization's donor management platform.
* Prepares deposits and maintains accurate supporting documentation.
* Coordinates deposit preparation with the Animal Care Manager to ensure cash and checks are independently counted and deposit totals verified before submission.
* Does not assume responsibility for the Board Treasurer's financial oversight or the bookkeeper's accounting and reconciliation responsibilities.

Facility and Vehicle Maintenance

* Ensures the shelter facility, buildings, grounds, and vehicles are maintained in a safe, sanitary, and functional condition.
* Regularly inspects shelter property to identify needed repairs, maintenance, and safety improvements.
* Coordinates necessary maintenance, repairs, and service work for buildings, grounds, equipment, and the shelter-owned vehicle.
* Coordinates outside contractors and service providers as needed.
* Monitors facility maintenance needs and communicates significant repairs, expenses, or safety concerns to the Board President or Vice President.
* Maintains records of facility maintenance, repairs, and vehicle servicing.
* Ensures appropriate safety and sanitation standards are maintained throughout the facility in collaboration with the Animal Care Manager.
* Coordinates maintenance of equipment and supplies necessary for daily shelter operations.

Customer Service and Public Relations

* Oversees customer service standards and ensures inquiries from the public are handled professionally and in a timely manner.
* Addresses customer complaints, concerns, and escalated issues involving shelter operations and services.
* Ensures staff communicate shelter policies and procedures accurately and consistently.
* Oversees the administrative aspects of public inquiries, including adoption-related communications and follow-up.
* Works with the Animal Care Manager to ensure adoption applicants receive timely communication and accurate information.
* Supports positive relationships with municipal partners, community organizations, donors, volunteers, and the public.

Safety, Compliance, and Incident Reporting

Safety and Incident Reporting

* Ensures workplace safety policies and procedures are implemented and followed by all employees and volunteers throughout shelter operations.
* Identifies and addresses potential safety hazards involving employees, volunteers, visitors, animals, facilities, vehicles, and shelter operations.
* Ensures appropriate safety procedures are followed regarding hazardous materials, chemicals, equipment, and other workplace hazards.
* Completes and maintains administrative incident documentation as necessary.
* Oversees reporting and follow-up for operational incidents involving employees, volunteers, visitors, facilities, vehicles, and shelter operations, in coordination with the Animal Care Manager when animal care is involved.
* Ensures required incident reports are completed, appropriate notifications are made, and corrective or follow-up actions are addressed.
* Ensures significant workplace injuries, animal-related incidents, bites, escapes, safety concerns, regulatory issues, and operational emergencies are promptly communicated to the Board President or Vice President.
* Works collaboratively with the Animal Care Manager to investigate incidents, identify contributing factors, and implement appropriate corrective measures.

Cross-Training and Operational Coverage

* Develops and maintains working knowledge of the Animal Care Manager's essential responsibilities to provide operational coverage during absences, vacations, or other staffing needs.
* Cross-trains with the Animal Care Manager on essential animal care procedures, shelter operations, animal-related recordkeeping, and other responsibilities necessary to maintain continuity of operations.
* Provides reasonable assistance with animal care and other responsibilities outside the primary area of administrative and operational oversight when necessary to maintain shelter operations.
* Coordinates with the Animal Care Manager to ensure ongoing responsibilities, outstanding issues, and time-sensitive matters are communicated and addressed during periods of absence.
* When providing coverage, operates within established policies, procedures, and delegated authority. Veterinary and medical decisions must remain within the scope of appropriate veterinary direction and professional judgment.
* Retains overall operational authority and coordinates decisions requiring management oversight during periods when the Animal Care Manager is unavailable.
* Communicates significant decisions, operational concerns, and matters requiring additional authority to the Board President and Vice President.

Reporting and Board Communication

* Provides regular updates regarding shelter operations, staffing, administrative matters, facility needs, and significant operational concerns.
* Prepares and submits operational reports for monthly Board meetings.
* Serves as the primary management contact for routine operational communication with the Board President and Vice President.
* Communicates significant changes in staffing, operational needs, and facility conditions to the Board President and Vice President.
* Assists with the development and implementation of organizational policies, procedures, and operational improvements.
* Maintains appropriate confidentiality regarding employee, applicant, donor, financial, and organizational information.
* Other duties as assigned by the Board President and Vice President.

AUTHORITY AND REPORTING RELATIONSHIP

The Shelter Manager serves as the senior operational manager of Animal Orphanage and reports directly to the President and Vice President of the Board of Directors.

The Shelter Manager has overall responsibility for the daily operation of the shelter and final day-to-day decision-making authority regarding operational priorities, staffing and scheduling, administrative matters, customer service, facility operations, and coordination between departments, subject to established organizational policies, approved budgets, and the authority of the Board of Directors.

The Animal Care Manager reports directly to the Shelter Manager and has primary responsibility and decision-making authority over daily animal care operations and the direction of animal care staff within established policies and veterinary guidance.

The Shelter Manager is responsible for coordinating the work of both management positions, resolving operational disagreements, and ensuring organizational priorities are met. This authority does not eliminate the Animal Care Manager's responsibility or professional judgment regarding animal welfare and daily animal care practices. Veterinary medical decisions must remain consistent with veterinary direction.

Significant animal welfare, safety, regulatory, personnel, financial, or other organizational concerns must be elevated to the Board President or Vice President as appropriate. The Board retains authority over organizational governance, policies, budgets, and major personnel decisions.

HOURS

40 hours per week. Regular schedule is 7:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Hours may occasionally vary based on operational needs. Hours may not be flexed prior to 7:00 a.m., with the exception of days requiring early morning operational responsibilities.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE

Shelter Operations: Knowledge of animal shelter operations, applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, ordinances, policies, and procedures relevant to the operation of an animal shelter.

Supervision and Human Resources: Knowledge of leadership techniques, principles, and procedures to recruit, train, supervise, schedule, evaluate, and manage employees. Knowledge of employee relations, performance management, and workplace policies.

Financial and Administrative Management: Knowledge of basic accounting principles, purchasing procedures, expense tracking, payroll coordination, recordkeeping, and administrative practices.

Facility and Safety Management: Knowledge of occupational hazards, safety precautions, facility maintenance practices, and applicable safety regulations related to maintaining a safe and sanitary workplace.

Customer Service: Knowledge of principles and processes for providing professional customer service, establishing service standards, resolving complaints, and maintaining positive relationships with the public.

REQUIRED SKILLS

Computer Skills: Proficiency with personal computers, word processing, spreadsheets, email, website administration, shelter management software, and related programs.

Judgment and Decision Making: Ability to evaluate operational needs, establish priorities, anticipate potential problems, and make sound decisions within the scope of assigned responsibilities.

Interpersonal Relationships: Ability to develop and maintain cooperative and professional relationships with employees, board members, volunteers, vendors, municipal representatives, and other organizations.

Organization: Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities, maintain accurate records, meet deadlines, and coordinate competing operational priorities.

Compassion: Demonstrated compassion and respect toward animals and the people who care for them. A genuine commitment to the humane philosophy and mission of Animal Orphanage is essential.

Physical Stamina: Ability to perform occasional moderately physically demanding work, including climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, crouching, and lifting, carrying, pushing, or pulling objects and materials weighing 20–50 pounds.

REQUIRED ABILITIES

Communication: Excellent ability to communicate complex ideas and proposals effectively, both verbally and in writing. Ability to prepare reports, policies, procedures, and other administrative documents. Ability to listen, understand, and communicate sensitive information with tact, diplomacy, and confidentiality.

Coordination of Work: Ability to establish and implement effective administrative programs and procedures, prioritize competing responsibilities, manage schedules, and coordinate the work of multiple employees.

Financial Management: Ability to perform arithmetic, algebraic, and basic statistical applications to complete purchasing and financial transactions. Ability to understand and apply basic accounting principles and practices in the review and reporting of budget and expense information.

Leadership: Ability to provide direction, establish expectations, address performance concerns, resolve operational disagreements, and foster a professional, accountable, and cooperative workplace.

Problem Solving: Ability to identify operational challenges, evaluate available options, and implement practical solutions while recognizing when Board direction or approval is necessary.

ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES

Performance of essential functions may require exposure to adverse environmental conditions, including dirt, dust, pollen, odors, wetness, humidity, weather and temperature extremes, noise, hazardous materials, traffic hazards, bright or dim lighting, toxic agents, animal or wildlife attacks, animal and human bites, disease, pathogenic substances, and rude or irate customers.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

* High school diploma required. College-level coursework in business administration, management, human resources, or a related field preferred.
* Certificate or degree in business administration, management, or a related field preferred.
* Five years of experience in administrative, operational, or organizational management preferred.
* Two to three years of supervisory and administrative experience preferred.
* Experience in animal shelter operations or a nonprofit organization preferred.
* Demonstrated experience in staff supervision, scheduling, administrative recordkeeping, customer service, and operational coordination.
* Must have excellent oral and written communication skills.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

* Acceptable general background check, including local and state criminal history checks and sex offender registry check.
* Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
* Satisfactory results from a pre-employment medical evaluation.

Title: Director — BAU (Business-As-Usual), Payroll & SaaS Operations
Description:
**We're Hiring**

**Director — BAU (Business-As-Usual), Payroll & SaaS Operations**

*Re-engineer a global payroll operation: platform-led, offshore-first, automated, advisory.*

**Department:**
Payroll & SaaS

**Reports To:**
Initially the Group CEO; transitioning to the Business Unit Managing Director

**Location:**
Dubai, UAE (onsite preferred); hybrid considered for the right candidate. Travel required.

**About Mercans**

Mercans is a global workforce solutions company. Through technology-led payroll and SaaS services, we help organizations pay and manage their people across borders — compliantly and at scale. We are re-engineering how our global payroll operation runs, and this role leads that transformation.

**The Opportunity**

**This is a hands-on transformation role, not a back-office management one.**
We are looking for a leader to re-engineer Mercans' managed-payroll operation into a country-agnostic, offshore-first, product-led model — one where country knowledge lives in the platform and a central compliance center of excellence rather than in individuals, where automation and AI remove manual work, and where customers own and control their data and execution through self-service. The goal is a standardized run-cycle where any consultant can run any payroll anywhere, and an operation that partners with clients strategically rather than just processing their payroll.

**This is a hands-on, grass-roots role.**
You will learn the product deeply, get close to clients and the operation, resolve issues at the grass-root level, and lead by doing rather than delegating. You will report initially to the Group CEO and, in due course, to the Business Unit Managing Director.

**What You'll Own**

Your mission is to deliver a new operating model. You will:

1. **Build a country-agnostic operating model**
   — codify country rules and knowledge into the platform and a central compliance center of excellence, with one standardized run-cycle and no single-expert dependency.
2. **Build an offshore-first, fungible workforce**
   — cross-trained and “2-deep” in every country, delivering high productivity at scale.
3. **Put customers in control**
   — self-service and data ownership through the product, and a strategic, advisory relationship instead of support ping-pong.
4. **Automate relentlessly**
   — automate manual and country-variable steps, deploy AI as a knowledge layer, and use anomaly detection for visibility and quality.
5. **Run a leaner, focused delivery core**
   with disciplined quality and performance governance.
6. **Migrate all clients onto a single platform**
   to eliminate manual processes and enable people to move freely between clients.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Country-Agnostic, Platform-Led Operating Model**

* Relocate country knowledge out of individuals into the platform (codified rules, wage-type catalogs, formulas) and a central compliance center of excellence.
* Establish one standardized, country-agnostic run-cycle so any consultant can run any payroll anywhere, eliminating single-expert dependency.
* Migrate all clients onto a single platform to remove manual processes and enable free movement of people between clients.

**Offshore-First, Fungible Workforce**

* Make offshore the primary delivery model; cross-train so no client depends on a single person and every country is “2-deep.”
* Drive consultant productivity toward best-in-class levels at scale.

**Customer Experience, Self-Service & Data Ownership**

* Give customers ownership and control of their data, timelines, and execution through self-service.
* Shift client engagement from tactical execution to a strategic, advisory partnership, and drive changes to customer data toward zero for compliance.

**Automation & AI**

* Automate every manual and country-variable step (statutory reports, integrations, bank files, and more) using a deliberate map → automate → internalize approach.
* Deploy AI as an on-demand knowledge layer and anomaly-detection tooling for visibility and quality.

**Scope, Quality & Performance Governance**

* Run a leaner, focused managed-payroll delivery core with clear scope discipline.
* Stand up a business-assurance / QA function with process audits, SLA monitoring, a regional RAG on stability, scalability, and resilience, and a disciplined review, coaching, and appraisal cadence.

**How You'll Work — Hands-On & Grass-Roots**

* Learn the product and the operation first-hand, stay close to clients, and resolve issues at root cause rather than delegating.

**What You'll Bring**

* **Hands-on and grass-roots by nature —**
  you learn the product deeply, get close to clients and operations, and resolve issues at root-cause level rather than delegating.
* **Operating-model transformation —**
  proven design and delivery of a standardized, offshore-first, platform-led payroll/operations model that removes country-knowledge and single-expert dependency.
* **Automation and AI expertise —**
  process standardization, product adoption, automation, and applied AI (including agentic AI) to eliminate manual work.
* **A customer-advisory and self-service orientation —**
  you move clients to self-service and strategic partnership, delivering an unparalleled client experience.
* **Operations leadership at scale —**
  10+ years in global payroll outsourcing or SaaS operations, including multi-regional and offshore delivery leadership.
* **Technology and compliance fluency —**
  deep understanding of payroll/SaaS platforms, config-driven operations, integrations, and multi-country payroll compliance.
* **Leadership and resilience —**
  proven ability to coach teams, influence stakeholders at all levels, and stay composed under pressure.
* **Education —**
  Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations Management, or a related field; MBA preferred.

**What Success Looks Like**

In your first 12–18 months, success means:

* A standardized, country-agnostic run-cycle is live — any consultant can run any payroll anywhere, with no single-expert dependency.
* Delivery is offshore-first and “2-deep,” with strong consultant productivity.
* Customers self-serve and own their data, and the relationship is strategic and advisory — with excellent CSAT and retention.
* Manual and country-variable steps are automated, and clients are migrated onto a single platform.
* The delivery core is leaner and well-governed, with clean compliance and strong quality assurance.

**Why Mercans**

* Lead a genuine transformation of a global operation at the center of how the world pays its people.
* A real mandate to re-engineer the model — this is a role for a builder, not a caretaker.
* A global, fast-moving, technology-led environment with a direct line to senior leadership.
* Competitive compensation aligned to the seniority and impact of the role.

**How to Apply**

To apply, please submit your CV and a short note outlining an operation you have transformed through the Mercans careers portal. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

*Mercans is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce.*

Title: Senior Information Systems Manager
Description:
### **About Us**

For over 90 years, Healthcare & Municipal Employees' Credit Union (HMECU) has proudly served healthcare, municipal, fire, and police communities across Ontario. We are committed to helping our members achieve financial wellbeing through trusted advice, exceptional service, and meaningful relationships.

At HMECU, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our purpose — **We care for the financial needs and wellbeing of our members so you can focus on what matters most** — we are building a culture focused on growth, innovation, accountability, and member impact.

### **Position Summary**

The Senior Information Systems Manager is HMECU’s senior technical authority, accountable for the effective operation, security, reliability and continuous improvement of the Credit Union’s information technology and information systems. Reporting to the Chief Operations & Digital Officer (CODO), the Manager provides expert technical leadership, proactively recommends technology strategy and priorities, and develops and executes an annual IT work plan and longer-term roadmap aligned with organizational objectives and regulatory obligations.

In HMECU’s lean operating environment, this is both a leadership and hands-on delivery role. The Manager is expected to independently identify needs and risks, develop practical plans, carry out technical and administrative work, coordinate external service providers where appropriate, and lead initiatives through implementation, documentation, testing, adoption and ongoing monitoring. The role serves as a key technical advisor and contributor across the organization.

  

### **Job Responsibilities**

### **Technology Leadership, Planning and Delivery**

* Act as HMECU's senior technical subject-matter expert; assess technology needs and recommend practical, secure and cost-effective solutions.
* Develop and execute an annual IT work plan and multi-year technology roadmap addressing system lifecycles, security, compliance, audits, projects and continuous improvement.
* Own initiatives from requirements and planning through implementation, testing, documentation, adoption and post-implementation review.
* Anticipate technology, regulatory and operational requirements and proactively recommend priorities, solutions, and risk mitigation strategies.
* Partner with business leaders and the Senior Business Analyst to translate business requirements into sustainable systems, process improvements, integrations and data solutions.

### **Information Security, Risk and Audit Readiness**

* Serve as HMECU’s Information Security Manager unless otherwise designated, fulfilling responsibilities assigned under HMECU's Information Security Policy and related standards.
* Translate security policies, technical standards and regulatory requirements into practical controls, procedures and implementation plans.
* Implement and verify security controls, including access management, authentication, endpoint and network protection, vulnerability management, patching and secure configuration.
* Maintain audit and regulatory review readiness, including evidence, gap assessments, remediation plans and reporting.
* Act as the first-line operational owner of technology and information security risks: identify and assess exposures, implement and monitor controls, maintain risk and remediation records, report control effectiveness and support independent review and challenge by risk management and internal audit.
* Develop, maintain and regularly test IT disaster recovery and incident response procedures aligned with HMECU’s broader business continuity framework.
* Ensure timely identification, assessment, documentation and escalation of material IT incidents; support authorized management in meeting applicable regulatory notification requirements, conducting post-incident reviews and completing corrective actions.

### **IT Operations, Infrastructure and Service Delivery**

* Ensure dependable daily operation, maintenance, monitoring, troubleshooting and support of HMECU’s infrastructure, networks, endpoints, applications, integrations and core technology services; perform work directly when needed.
* Manage service requests, incidents, system changes, access administration and technical documentation, ensuring timely follow-through and communication.
* Administer or oversee user provisioning, access changes, periodic access reviews and deprovisioning across relevant systems, with appropriate approvals and segregation of duties.
* Lead IT change management processes, including change assessment, approvals, testing, implementation, rollback planning and records.
* Maintain technology asset inventories, lifecycle and replacement plans, licensing, backups and operational procedures.
* Oversee HMECU’s ATM technology, including availability, technical support, vendor coordination, upgrades, security and operational continuity.

### **Projects, Emerging Technology and Artificial Intelligence**

* Lead the technical assessment, design, implementation and integration of technology projects, including coordination of vendors, testing, conversion, deployment and operational handover.
* Proactively assess emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, and recommend suitable use cases, solutions and implementation approaches.
* Lead technical enablement and ongoing management of approved AI tools and other emerging technologies, ensuring alignment with HMECU’s AI Policy, privacy and information security requirements, and supporting employee adoption and training in partnership with business owners.

### **Vendor, Financial and Resource Management**

* Own the operational performance and delivery of HMECU’s managed IT service provider and assigned technology vendors, including service expectations, issue escalation, follow-up and verification of completed work.
* Contribute technical expertise and evidence to third-party risk assessments, contract reviews, procurement decisions, renewals and technology dependencies; track required vendor actions.
* Develop, manage and monitor the IT operating and capital budgets; forecast technology spending, renewals and project costs, identify efficiencies and explain variances and investment needs.
* Plan and prioritize available resources realistically, personally undertaking technical, administrative and implementation work where no internal IT resource is available.

### **Governance, Privacy and Organizational Collaboration**

* Participate as a member of HMECU’s Privacy Committee, providing technical advice, supporting privacy risk assessments, and implementing assigned technology and security actions in coordination with the designated Privacy Officer.
* Ensure technology practices and deliverables support applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies and approved governance frameworks; provide accurate, timely reporting and recommendations to management and committees.
* Work constructively with staff and leaders across HMECU to resolve issues, communicate technology changes, support training and promote responsible use of information systems.

### **Minimum Requirements**

* 8–10 years of relevant information technology experience, preferably including at least 3 years managing an IT function or comparable end-to-end technical accountability.
* Bachelor’s degree in information technology or a related field; an advanced degree or relevant professional certifications are assets.
* Demonstrated hands-on capability across IT operations, infrastructure, security controls, incident management, system administration and vendor-supported environments.
* Experience translating policies, standards, audit findings and technical requirements into implemented procedures, controls, evidence and completed remediation.
* Strong planning, prioritization, problem-solving, project delivery and communication skills, including the ability to present clear recommendations, alternatives, risks and progress to management.
* Experience in a regulated financial services environment, IT audit, security frameworks, privacy or emerging technology/AI governance is an asset.
* SQL skills and related technical certifications are assets.

Title: Director, Business Technology & Transformation
Description:
North America Construction (1993) Ltd. – NAC Constructors Ltd. (NAC) is well known for our expertise in water and wastewater construction across Canada. Our self-performing team of almost 500 skilled professionals and experts in trades and engineering, comprehensively handles projects, from conceptualization to delivery. We also have extensive experience in fields such as civil, structural, process mechanical, building mechanical, electrical and instrumentation work. At NAC, our priority is to maintain the highest level of quality and safety. The depth of our resources is evident in the variety of projects we construct; from water filtration to wastewater treatment; dams to ethanol; we build it all….and more!

Bring your construction industry knowledge and technology leadership experience to NAC, where you’ll have the opportunity to shape our technology strategy, modernize business systems, and drive meaningful business transformation.

North America Construction (NAC) is looking for a business-minded technology leader who understands the demands of a construction or project-based environment and can translate technology into practical business improvements.

Reporting to the VP, Corporate Services, you will lead NAC’s technology strategy, manage a small internal technology team, and oversee external providers. Working closely with executive leadership and teams across finance, operations, estimating, HR, equipment, and projects, you will improve business systems, decision-making, productivity, and the employee experience.

### **Position Responsibilities:**

**Technology Strategy & Governance**

* Maintain a technology and transformation roadmap aligned with corporate priorities and business objectives.
* Establish technology governance, standards, policies and decision-making processes.
* Manage budgets and investment plans, assess emerging technologies, and develop and present business cases to executive leadership.

**Enterprise Applications**

* Provide strategic direction for NAC’s enterprise applications, including ERP platforms, Jonas Construction Software, Procore, Primavera P6, Concur, HR systems, equipment and fleet systems, and future applications.
* Lead or oversee enterprise system implementations, integrations, modernization and enhancements, including requirements definition, vendor management, implementation planning, change management and user adoption. Ensure systems are effectively integrated, aligned with business processes, and support operational efficiency and NAC's evolving business needs.

**Data & Analytics**

* Lead data governance, stewardship, business intelligence and reporting capabilities, including Power BI, executive dashboards, consistent KPIs, and data warehouse and reporting architecture.
* Ensure teams have access to reliable, timely and actionable information to support operational, financial and strategic decision-making.

**Digital Workplace, Automation & AI**

* Lead digital workplace strategy, governance, and adoption across Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, Teams, Power Platform, and Copilot.
* Lead the planning, governance and adoption of AI and emerging technologies, including Microsoft Copilot, workflow automation, knowledge management and collaboration tools. Identify opportunities to improve productivity and business efficiency through effective implementation, change management and employee adoption.

**Business Transformation & Process Improvement**

* Partner with business leaders to identify, prioritize and lead company-wide transformation initiatives and technology-enabled process improvements.
* Lead initiatives to simplify workflows, reduce manual and administrative effort, and improve productivity and operational effectiveness. Work with business leaders to establish, measure, and evaluate the benefits and outcomes of these initiatives.

**Technology Operations, Cybersecurity & Team Leadership**

* Provide strategic oversight of technology operations, infrastructure planning, managed service providers, service levels, cybersecurity, technology risk, business continuity and disaster recovery. Ensure technology services are secure, reliable and aligned with business needs and NAC's growth.
* Lead and manage NAC's internal technology team, establishing priorities, delegating responsibilities, coaching and developing team members, and ensuring effective coordination with external service providers.
* Ensure NAC has the appropriate resources, expertise, governance and controls to support its technology environment. Maintain overall accountability for technology performance, service delivery, operational reliability and risk management, whether delivered internally or through external providers.

### **Qualifications:**

* Post-secondary degree or diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, Engineering, Information Systems or a related discipline preferred. Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience will be considered.
* Relevant professional certifications in project management, business analysis, IT service management, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture or organizational change management are considered assets.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in technology leadership, business systems, enterprise applications, digital transformation or business technology, with increasing responsibility for strategy, delivery and organizational outcomes.
* Demonstrated experience leading technology functions, internal teams, external service providers and enterprise-wide initiatives.
* Experience in construction, engineering, infrastructure, manufacturing or other project-based organizations strongly preferred.
* Proven experience developing and executing enterprise technology strategies, roadmaps, governance frameworks and investment plans aligned with business objectives.
* Demonstrated experience leading ERP implementations, enterprise application modernization, system integrations and business systems optimization.
* Strong understanding of enterprise architecture, data management, business intelligence, analytics and executive reporting.
* Experience leading enterprise business intelligence, data visualization and analytics platforms, such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, Domo or comparable solutions. Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise reporting frameworks, executive dashboards, consistent KPIs and data governance practices that support operational, financial and strategic decision-making.
* Demonstrated success leading technology-enabled business transformation, process improvement and organizational change initiatives, with a focus on measurable business outcomes.
* Experience overseeing IT operations, infrastructure, cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity and disaster recovery planning.
* Familiarity with AI, automation, Microsoft Copilot and emerging technologies, including their practical business applications, governance considerations and organizational adoption.
* Strong business acumen and financial awareness, with the ability to develop business cases, evaluate technology investments and assess their business value.
* Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management and change leadership skills, including the ability to translate complex technology concepts into practical business recommendations and outcomes.

**By the end of your first 24 months, you will have:**

* Established and implemented a clear enterprise technology and business transformation roadmap aligned with NAC's corporate priorities.
* Strengthened technology governance, investment planning and executive decision-making, while building strong business-wide relationships.
* Improved the effectiveness, integration and adoption of key enterprise applications and advanced the modernization of NAC's business systems.
* Expanded adoption of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Power Platform and Copilot, supported by appropriate governance and employee adoption.
* Strengthened company-wide reporting, analytics, data governance and executive visibility into business performance.
* Identified and delivered meaningful improvements through automation, workflow redesign and technology-enabled process transformation.
* Strengthened cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity, disaster recovery and overall operational reliability.
* Established a well-managed technology function with clear accountability, effective external partnerships and the capabilities required to support NAC's future growth.

  
  

**NAC Offers:**

* Competitive compensation
* Opportunities for career growth, development and advancement, including financial assistance
* Comprehensive benefit plan (dental, vision, health, etc.)
* Employee & Family Assistance Program
* Excellent company matched pension plan
* Registered Retirement Savings Plans
* Additional time off between Christmas and New Year’s Day
* Community involvement opportunities
* Friendly working environment
* Numerous team activities and various company events

Title: Manager, Educational Technology
Description:
Reporting to the Director, Academic Quality and Teaching Innovation, the Manager, Educational Technology provides leadership and oversight vis-à-vis the SLATE (Sheridan's Teaching and Learning Environment) environment as well as broader educational technology strategy.

The incumbent is accountable for all operational aspects of SLATE, which operates for all Sheridan users on a continuous 24x7x365 basis. In this capacity the incumbent provides leadership for the administration, design, development, training, and support functions associated with SLATE as well as other integrated learning technologies, e-learning and digital innovation. This includes any internal integrations to Sheridan's infrastructure including but not limited to student information systems (SIS), HR systems, authentication services and other leveraged systems.

This position collaborates pan-institutionally to engage a wide range of key partners at Sheridan, i.e. Academic Division, IT, OTR, as it relates to planning, strategy, and operationalization of educational technologies, including but not limited to SLATE. The position engages and contributes to provincial and sector educational technology bodies. Further, the role is a key interface with educational technology vendors to ensure the provisioned tools are meeting the broader educational and pedagogical needs of the Sheridan teaching and learning community.

**What You’ll Be Doing**

* Managing system administration for SLATE and associated learning technologies, leading teams to improve the experience of faculty, students, and employees.
* Plans and assesses upgrades, patches, and pilots of new features; oversees the e-learning design and digital innovation teams; and advises the Director on the development and review of programs and services.
* Evaluating emerging technologies and, with the Director, builds business cases for adopting them, while managing the life cycle of learning technologies from onboarding to retirement.
* Managing major cross-College projects, supports budget and strategic planning, maintains policies, documentation, and usage statistics, and is accountable for timely, accurate communications.
* Managing vendor, sector, and internal partnerships through negotiating contracts, master agreements, SLAs, and End User License Agreements (EULA)s for all contracted services, including cloud-based services, and administers breach procedures such as responses to service disruptions.
* Maintaining relationships with account managers and other vendor representatives, stays apprised of product and service roadmaps, and leads vendor crisis management when service is disrupted or degraded.
* Providing leadership, strategic direction, and supervision to SLATE staff and other digital learning teams, ensuring adequate coverage, prompt response to user support requests, and proper escalation of issues to internal resources or vendors, with all issues documented and tracked to resolution.
* Hiring, supervising, coaching, and managing staff performance in compliance with the Collective Agreement, keeps certifications and training current, and recommends professional development aligned with Sheridan’s strategic vision, while fostering a safe, respectful, and inclusive work environment.
* Accountable for resource stewardship and compliance with Sheridan policies, legislation, and agreements, including Health and Safety, Human Rights, AODA, Acceptable Use, and WHMIS, as well as the secure management of records and confidential information under Sheridan’s Records and Information Management Policy.
* Ensuring the delivery of standard and ad hoc instructions and information on the use of learning technologies, including SLATE procedures, and prepares reports and presentations on SLATE, pilot projects, and other educational technologies for decision-making groups.
* Serves on committees and cross-organizational teams that need expertise in teaching and learning technology or input on SLATE implementation for other Sheridan initiatives, and represents the portfolio’s interests on institutional working groups such as legal, privacy, and web governance.
* Leads project teams, analyzing requirements, developing plans, scheduling resources, and tracking and reporting on deliverables to senior leadership.
* Performing additional responsibilities, projects and initiatives, as required.

**About You**

You have a sound understanding of the **post-secondary education landscape**, including the challenges, emerging trends and issues shaping the sector, and can translate this knowledge into forward-thinking academic leadership.

You are deeply committed to **academic excellence and student success** and are passionate about creating high-quality learning experiences that prepare students to thrive in their studies, careers and communities.

You are an **exceptional communicator** with strong verbal, written and **presentation skills**, and can communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively with a variety of audiences.

You are a **collaborative and inclusive leader** with exceptional **relationship-building and interpersonal skills**. You inspire trust, engage others and build strong relationships that enable teams and individuals to succeed.

You have strong **organizational and managerial skills** and the ability to **multi-task, prioritize and manage multiple complex and competing demands**, while maintaining focus on broader strategic and operational priorities.

You exercise sound **judgement**, and your strong **problem-solving and conflict resolution skills**, coupled with your openness to new ways of thinking, allow you to navigate complex challenges and develop creative solutions that advance organizational goals.

You demonstrate a strong understanding of **cultural diversity** and the varied experiences and needs of diverse populations and are committed to creating learning and working environments where individuals feel **welcomed, respected and supported**.

You demonstrate a strong commitment to **equity, diversity, inclusion and belonging** and to fostering an educational and employment environment that removes barriers and creates equitable opportunities for individuals to participate, contribute and succeed.

**The ideal candidate will also possess the following qualifications:**

* Master’s degree in educational technology, online learning, education or related field;
* 7 years of experience as a senior practitioner, technical advisor, consultant or supervisor with progressive experience in learning and educational technologies (software and hardware) (equivalencies to be considered)
* Operational knowledge of IT infrastructure which interface with learning and educational technologies
* Familiarity with cloud-based computing, enterprise applications and vendor management

* Experience managing staff in unionized environments

Every member of the Sheridan community is passionate about the transformational role we play in people’s lives. Our strategic plan, Sheridan 2027: Forging the Future (https://www.sheridancollege.ca/sheridan2027), charts a path towards a new ground-breaking model of higher education that reshapes post-secondary education and better prepares students for the future. We are committed to demonstrably advancing equity, diversity, and inclusivity. Diversity is our strength and fuels our commitment to excellence. Title: Senior Portfolio & Program Manager, Operational Technology & Controls
Description:
**Who are we?**
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.
  
  
A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.
  
  
A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Senior Portfolio & Program Manager, Operational Technology & Controls is responsible for the integrated portfolio of Operational Technology & Engineering (OT&E) initiatives across controls, central monitoring, OT infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, and automation, ensuring programs are sequenced, governed, funded, and transitioned to operations as one connected roadmap rather than as separate projects.
  
  
This role combines disciplined portfolio and program management with proven, hands-on expertise in industrial controls and operational technology, including how controls systems integrate across critical facilities. It does not replace technical owners: engineering owns design, architecture, and engineering acceptance, while this role owns portfolio governance, integration, and transition to operations, and recommends sequencing, funding, and prioritization decisions to leadership. This position collaborates with engineering, operations, cybersecurity, IT, network, architecture, finance, procurement, vendors, system integrators, and regional teams across Global Operations Excellence to deliver key initiatives such as GMCC and central SCADA, and to strengthen the reliability, security, and supportability of Equinix’s critical facilities.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Maintain a single, current view of all OT&E initiatives, including scope, funding, dependencies, risk, and expected value
* Run intake, scoring, and prioritization of new work against strategy, architectural standards, and capacity
* Lead quarterly and annual planning, roadmap development, and investment cases, partnering with Finance on forecasting and variance reporting
* Lead multi-team programs end to end, including integrated plans, critical paths, and phased global rollouts to site teams
* Define and enforce stage gates and readiness criteria (design, security review, pilot, production)

Title: Business Continuity Manager
Description:
**Position Summary**

The Business Continuity Manager is a key role responsible for overseeing the development and implementation of business continuity plans to ensure the company’s operations can withstand and recover from unexpected disruptions.

**What will your job entail?**

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Assess the potential impact of disruptions on critical business processes, identifying dependencies, recovery time objectives (RTOs), and resource requirements.
* Identify and evaluate risks that could affect business operations, including natural disasters, cyber threats, supply chain disruptions, and other emergencies. Develop strategies to mitigate these risks.
* Create and maintain comprehensive emergency response plans that outline procedures for handling crises, evacuations, communication, and resource allocation during disruptions.
* Develop and update business continuity plans (BCPs) that address various scenarios, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and compliance requirements.
* Coordinate regular testing and exercises to validate BCP effectiveness. Conduct tabletop simulations, functional exercises, and full-scale drills to assess readiness.
* Work closely with cross-functional teams, including IT, facilities, legal, and senior management, to ensure alignment and buy-in for business continuity efforts.
* Provide training sessions to employees on BCPs, emergency procedures, and their roles during disruptions. Foster a culture of preparedness and awareness.
* Regularly review and enhance business continuity strategies based on lessons learned, industry best practices, and changes in the business environment.  
    
  **Work Experience and Education:**
* Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management or Business with 6+ years of experience
* 3+ years of supervisor or lead experience.
* Insurance industry experience preferred

**Licenses &** **Certifications:**

Certified Business Continuity Professional (CBCP) or ISO 22301 Lead Implementer or Project Management Professional (PMP) is preferred

**Technical/Functional Skills:**

* Risk assessment and risk management: Identifies, analyzes, and prioritizes operational, technology, third-party, and environmental risks, and develops practical risk mitigation strategies aligned with enterprise risk management frameworks.
* Business impact analysis (BIA): Conducts BIAs to determine critical processes, dependencies, recovery time objectives (RTOs), recovery point objectives (RPOs), maximum tolerable downtime, and financial and operational impacts of disruption.
* Business continuity and resilience planning: Develops and maintains business continuity plans, crisis management and emergency response plans, and recovery strategies in line with ISO 22301, DRI International, or Business Continuity Institute (BCI) standards and practices.
* Strategic planning: Builds multi-year business continuity program roadmaps, defines program metrics, and aligns continuity priorities with business strategy and operational resilience goals.
* IT disaster recovery and technology resilience: Partners with IT and information security to align application recovery priorities, system dependencies, and disaster recovery capabilities with business recovery requirements.
* Third-party and vendor continuity: Evaluates the resilience of critical vendors, service providers, and delegated authority partners, including review of vendor continuity plans and recovery capabilities.
* Business continuity software administration: Administers and configures business continuity planning platforms to manage plans, BIAs, contact data, assessments, and reporting.
* Mass notification and threat intelligence administration: Manages emergency notification systems, including contact data quality, message templates, and delivery testing, and monitors threat intelligence sources to provide timely alerts on severe weather, safety, and other events affecting employees and operations.
* Exercise design and facilitation: Designs, facilitates, and documents tabletop, functional, and full-scale exercises, and tracks resulting corrective actions through to completion.
* Data analysis and reporting: Analyzes plan, exercise, and incident data to draw clear conclusions, and produces dashboards and metrics that inform decisions by leadership.
* Presentation development and delivery: Develops and delivers clear, concise presentations and training materials to audiences ranging from front-line employees to senior executives.

**Functional Requirements:**

* Own the enterprise business continuity program lifecycle, including governance, policy and standards, annual plan review and approval cycles, and program maintenance across all business units.
* Lead and maintain the BIA process for all business units, and ensure results drive recovery strategies, resource requirements, and plan content.
* Maintain business continuity, crisis management, and emergency response plans, and verify that plan owners review and update them at least annually and after significant organizational or operational change.
* Plan and execute an annual schedule of exercises and tests, and document results, gaps, and corrective actions with assigned owners and due dates.
* Coordinate the organization’s response during incidents and disruptions, including activating plans, convening the crisis management team, and supporting internal and external communications.
* Conduct post-incident and post-exercise reviews, and incorporate lessons learned into plans, training, and program improvements.
* Ensure the program meets applicable insurance regulatory, contractual, and audit requirements, such as state department of insurance expectations, NAIC guidance, and client or carrier due diligence requests.
* Support client, carrier, regulator, and auditor inquiries by providing business continuity attestations, evidence, and documentation.
* Report on program status, risks, exercise results, and key metrics to senior leadership, executive committees, and the board as required.
* Manage the business continuity planning and mass notification platforms, including user access, data accuracy, and regular testing.
* Develop and deliver business continuity awareness and training programs for employees, plan owners, and crisis management team members.
* Supervise or lead business continuity staff, contractors, and a network of plan owners and coordinators, setting priorities and providing direction and coaching.

**Behavioral Skills:**

* Effective communication: Communicates clearly and calmly in writing and verbally, tailoring messages for executives, technical teams, and employees, especially during high-pressure incidents.
* Interpersonal skills and influence: Builds trusted relationships and gains buy-in across departments, business units, and levels of leadership without relying on direct authority.
* Attention to detail: Maintains accurate, complete, and audit-ready plans, records, and contact data.
* Decision making: Makes timely, well-informed decisions with incomplete information and balances risk, cost, and operational impact.
* Problem-solving: Applies structured, analytical thinking to resolve complex issues and develop practical solutions.
* Leadership and accountability: Leads by example, follows through on commitments, and holds teams and plan owners accountable for deliverables.
* Continuous learning: Stays current on emerging threats, regulatory changes, and industry best practices, and applies new knowledge to improve the program.
* Emotional intelligence: Remains composed under pressure, shows empathy toward affected employees, and adapts communication style to different audiences and situations

* Improve efficiency: raise utilisation and lower cost per delivery without moving cost onto DSPs or associates.
* Build partner economics: shape DSP commercial models with Finance that work at every volume level, and lead the trade-off decisions.

The Senior Director is a key member of the Parks and Recreation senior leadership team and shares accountability, alongside the General Manager and fellow Senior Directors, for the overall leadership, performance and strategic direction of the division. Operating within a highly collaborative executive environment, the leadership team works collectively to establish priorities, guide decision-making, allocate resources and advance Council-approved objectives. While accountable for their assigned portfolio and serving as the section's lead representative for related Council, committee, media and stakeholder matters, Senior Directors are expected to adopt an enterprise-wide lens, balancing portfolio needs with the broader interests of the division, the City and the communities it serves. Through this collective leadership model, the team drives integrated solutions, organizational excellence and consistent service delivery across Parks and Recreation.

Toronto Parks and Recreation delivers services and spaces that enhance the quality of life for millions of residents. From neighbourhood parks and sports fields to trails, horticultural displays and public gathering spaces, Toronto's parks system is fundamental to creating vibrant, healthy and connected communities.

The City of Toronto is seeking a strategic and accomplished leader to serve as Senior Director, Parks Operations.

Reporting to the General Manager, Parks and Recreation, the Senior Director provides executive leadership for a broad and highly visible parks operations portfolio responsible for the maintenance, stewardship, safety and operational readiness of parks, facilities and public spaces across Toronto. Leading one of the division's largest operational teams, this role ensures residents experience clean, safe, accessible and well-maintained parks every day.

Leading through a team of Directors and multidisciplinary professionals, you will oversee complex operations delivered across diverse geographies, service areas and workforce groups. You will ensure resources, workforce capacity and service delivery models remain aligned with community needs while fostering a culture grounded in accountability, safety, service excellence and innovation.

A defining priority of this role is ensuring operational excellence is embedded across one of the largest municipal parks systems in North America. You will champion a culture of performance, responsiveness and continuous improvement, ensuring services are delivered consistently, public assets are stewarded effectively, and residents receive a high-quality experience across Toronto's parks and public spaces. Through strong leadership, clear accountability and a commitment to excellence, you will strengthen organizational performance and build public confidence in the services Parks Operations delivers every day.

Success in this role requires exceptional political acuity, sound judgment and strong relationship management skills. You will regularly engage with elected officials, bargaining agents, community partners, residents and stakeholder groups to resolve complex issues, respond to emerging concerns and maintain public confidence in the delivery of parks services across Toronto.

**What You Bring to the Role:**

1. Post-secondary education in Parks Management, Environmental Services, Engineering or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
2. Extensive senior leadership experience overseeing large-scale operations, maintenance, facilities, public works, parks or service delivery portfolios within a complex organization.
3. Significant experience leading large operational teams and diverse workforces in a unionized environment, including workforce planning, labour relations and organizational effectiveness initiatives.
4. Demonstrated expertise in operational governance, maintenance management, service standards, quality assurance, performance management and continuous improvement.
5. Experience managing significant operating budgets and aligning resources, workforce strategies and service priorities to achieve organizational objectives.
6. Proven ability to lead senior managers and multidisciplinary teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety and service excellence.
7. Demonstrated success operating in politically sensitive and highly visible environments requiring sound judgment, diplomacy and strong stakeholder management capabilities.
8. Experience presenting operational strategies, service issues and recommendations to senior leadership teams, elected officials, boards, committees and community stakeholders.
9. Experience building productive relationships with bargaining agents, community partners, residents and external stakeholders in support of service excellence and organizational goals.
10. Familiarity with applicable occupational health and safety, labour, regulatory and municipal legislation.

Title: Manager of Clinic Operations
Description:
